title: Mottle and the Sun-Moon Sprout
markdown:
Once upon a time, in the rustling mountain woods that hugged the hidden terraces of Ferncrown, there lived a young goblin named Mottle. Skin as green and soft as fresh moss. Eyes as wide and curious as a mushroom cap, always looking for the next interesting leaf or wiggly worm.

Every day he set off on quiet explorations with Sparky, a tiny dragonet no bigger than a robin, scales shimmering like a sapphire sky after rain. When Sparky puffed a little cloud of smoke, it smelled of toasted marshmallows, a scent that always made Mottle feel warm. He collected smooth grey stones that felt cool in his hands and listened to pine trees whispering secrets being shared by the wind. He was a little shy. When the chattering squirrels hurried, or the wise old badger grumbled his slow thoughtful grumbles, Mottle’s moss-green cheeks grew warm, and he tucked himself behind Sparky, feeling much safer there.

Until one day a sound like two grumpy bumblebees having a loud argument drifted from Ferncrown’s terraces. Much louder. Definitely grumbly. Mottle’s ears, usually tucked, perked. A flutter in his tummy wanted the cozy moss patch. Sparky nudged him with a tiny scaly snout and puffed encouraging marshmallow smoke.

Because of that squabble, they crept closer and peeked through a leafy curtain of ferns. Wizard Fitzwilliam, silvery beard twitching, and Witch Willow, dandelion-fluff hair vibrating, stood over a tiny rather sad-looking sprout, each pointing a long skinny finger.

“It is clearly a Moonpetal sprout. It needs cool refreshing morning dew from the north slope.”

“Nonsense and fiddle-dee-dee! It’s a Sunbeam tendril. Warm golden afternoon sunshine from the south. My herbs told me so.”

Mottle had seen sprouts near home. This one looked as if it needed a gentle drink and some friendly sun, not a debate. He wanted to melt into moss. Sparky puffed a determined plume, as if to say: you can do it.

Mottle, who usually spoke only when spoken to, stepped out. He cleared his throat, a small reedy sound. “Um, excuse me?”

They stopped. Stared. Cheeks warm, he tried to shrink to dewdrop size.

“Well, hello there, young goblin,” Willow said, softening, eyebrows still knitted.

“Indeed,” Fitzwilliam peered over round spectacles. “Who might you be, young sprout-watcher?”

Because of that question, Mottle managed, voice trembling a little, “I’m Mottle. And this is Sparky.” Sparky chirped a polite greeting and another marshmallow cloud. “I was just wondering if maybe it’s a Sun-Moon sprout?”

They looked at each other. At the drooping sprout. At Mottle. Willow’s slow delighted smile. Fitzwilliam’s beard stopped twitching.

“A Sun-Moon sprout. They do say those peculiar ones need a bit of both sun and dew.”

“The ancient texts mention a rather peculiar hybrid that flourishes with alternating sun and dew, and a touch of warmth from morning and afternoon. A keen eye for nature, young Mottle.”

Until finally he took a deep breath. He might sound silly. They might ignore him. The sprout drooped. He spoke again, still soft, now clear and steady: not a lecture, just the little plant between them, wanting both. Pine and marshmallow on the air. Leaves whispering something that felt like room enough to stay.

Ever since then, Mottle still collected smooth grey stones and still listened to whispering trees. He no longer hid behind Sparky. He walked with his head a little higher, curious eyes on the path, ready for whatever gentle adventures the woods might bring.
characters: Mottle (shy young goblin), Sparky (a marshmallow-smoke dragonet)
author: StoryGen Community
